dimension_assessments.summary: The core states the principal behaviors for document synchronization boundaries, UI routing, compatibility routing, chat intelligence, diagnostic packaging, startup ordering, and failure recovery.
Editor intelligence surfaces, read-only Chat LSP, diagnostic-to-chat packaging, workspace-edit preview, and restart/status capabilities are explicitly named.
Real/virtual document inputs and diagnostic/session/URI payloads are named, but concrete schemas, identity, lifecycle, validation, and invalidation outputs are incomplete.
Strong negative boundaries exist, but synchronization, per-surface routing, payload schema, and startup-failure contracts still leave consequential branches unspecified.
Registration-before-spawn and failure/status concepts are explicit, but document synchronization, startup failure, cancellation, retry, and recovery transitions are not fully deterministic.
The core excludes several false authorities and separates health domains, but does not assign every listed UI/routing surface to a precise authoritative producer.
LSP-specific versus adjacent owner boundaries and chat non-ownership are explicit, but the distinct-owner requirement lacks a per-surface ownership map.
Editor UI surfaces, Search/index/fallback systems, current owner documents, chat/assistant context, Problems, gutter, and status surfaces are identified as consumers or adjacent systems.
The core distinguishes healthy LSP from fallback/search state, defines degraded disclosure and Problems/status placement, preserves Error/Waiting/restart copy, and forbids UI-thread blocking.
Crash, timeout, diagnostic clearing, restart, backoff, logging, and UI states are covered, but startup cleanup and retry termination/reset semantics remain ambiguous.
No authorization, workspace-boundary, redaction, retention, or remote disclosure rules are stated for file URIs, virtual content, diagnostics, and session references entering chat.
Failure effects are required to reach diagnostics, Problems, gutter, status, and logs, but the event, ordering, consistency, and partial-failure contract is absent.
Restart action, backoff constants, status copy, and stderr tail are operationally useful, but timeout thresholds, retry limits, crash-loop policy, reset, and cancellation are unspecified.
UI-thread non-blocking and bounded backoff are explicit, but this core provides no latency budgets, queue/backpressure limits, diagnostic-volume behavior, or quantitative timeout thresholds.
Stale FileManager and Tiers vocabulary are explicitly compatibility-only, current owner routing is required, and independent health domains remain separate.
The specified validators prove plan preservation/indexing, while runtime behavior and failure/UI outcomes lack executable acceptance oracles in this core.

Builders retain consequential discretion over synchronization, routing ownership, virtual documents, payload validation, failed-startup cleanup, retry policy, privacy controls, and propagation consistency.

The principal unknowns are the exact synchronization state machine, owner routing map, virtual-document lifecycle, diagnostic schema binding, mark-versus-cleanup branch, restart termination, privacy boundary, and propagation ordering.
